It is worth noting though that the write buffer has an offset given to it
```
      %0 = hal.interface.constant.load[0] : i32
      %1 = hal.interface.constant.load[1] : i32
      %15 = arith.extui %0 : i32 to i64
      %16 = arith.extui %1 : i32 to i64
      %17 = arith.shli %16, %c32_i64 : i64
      %18 = arith.ori %15, %17 : i64
      %19 = arith.index_castui %18 {stream.alignment = 64 : index} : i64 to index
%47 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(2) type(storage_buffer) alignment(64) offset(%19) : memref<?x?xf32>{%24, %44}
      %base_buffer_4, %offset_5, %sizes_6:2, %strides_7:2 = memref.extract_strided_metadata %47 : memref<?x?xf32> -> memref<f32>, index, index, index, index, index
      call @mlp_external_f32_f32_f32_i32_i32_i32(%base_buffer, %c0, %base_buffer_0, %c0, %base_buffer_4, %c0, %2, %3, %4) : (memref<f32>, index, memref<f32>, index, memref<f32>, index, i32, i32, i32) -> ()
      return
 ```
 However, at runtime I do notice that the second call, has same result and lhs buffer

>@nirvedhmeshram can you try setting --iree-scheduling-optimize-bindings=false and try . At least that will unblock us for now.

Yes that worked!

This is working as intended - the offset is passed as %14 on the second dispatch and then that should be used as the offset in the `%3 = stream.binding.subspan %arg1[%arg3] : !stream.binding -> !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:tensor<?x?xf32>>{%0, %1}` (%arg3).
I'm guessing something in your pipeline is ignoring that offset.
